result.title: Backward-Consistent Diffusion Sampling for Sparsely Observed PDE Inverse Problems
result.summary: Recovering Partial Differential Equation (PDE) coefficient fields from extremely sparse observations is a severely ill-posed inverse problem for which generative machine learning methods (e.g., diffusion models) have become a leading way to encode the prior. Recent state-of-the-art diffusion solvers lift these priors to function spaces, finding a physics-consistent reconstruction in the output space of the diffusion denoiser. We prove that, in a discontinuous PDE setting, output space methods can result in failure to appropriately minimize the unobserved error with the correct coefficient field. Consequently, we propose Function space Backward-Consistent Sampling (FunBCS), an input space optimization approach for solving PDE problems which aims to find the best input such that the denoiser reconstruction is physics-consistent. We then prove that FunBCS appropriately minimizes the unobserved error, unlike output space optimization methods. Per our theoretical analysis, we also provide insights on how to dynamically allocate the number of input space optimization steps used throughout the sampling process. Our evaluations, across four PDE inverse problems (including the discontinuous Darcy flow), demonstrate that FunBCS reduces the reconstruction error by $27$-$64\%$ while running $1.4$-$2.1\times$ faster when compared to the current state-of-the-art.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究稀疏观测下的 PDE 逆问题，证明扩散模型输出空间优化在系数场不连续时可能无法正确减小未观测误差，并提出在输入空间做反向一致性采样的 FunBCS，配合动态分配优化步数，在四个 PDE 任务上降低误差并加速。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接视觉联系，但「输出空间 vs 输入空间」的误差可见性分析与按采样阶段动态分配优化步数的思路，可能为 latent 状态中证据是否被真正使用、以及 THINK 步数/计算预算分配提供类比线索，可供核查。
